title: Data Handling: Summarising and Interpreting Data
summary: Sampling and bias, grouped data, quartiles and interquartile range, box-and-whisker plots, comparing data sets, and identifying misleading statistics.

notes.text: A **population** is the whole group you want to know about; a **sample** is the part you actually survey. A good sample is **representative** (similar to the population) and large enough.

items: **Bias** happens when the sample is not representative, e.g. asking only people at a gym how often they exercise.
**Leading questions** push people to a particular answer, e.g. 'Don't you agree that taxes are too high?'
**Minimum** and **maximum**: the smallest and largest values.
**Lower quartile** ($Q_1$): the median of the lower half. **Upper quartile** ($Q_3$): the median of the upper half.
**Interquartile range** (IQR) $= Q_3 - Q_1$: the spread of the middle 50% of the data.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: Test marks: 34; 45; 52; 58; 61; 64; 70; 77; 85; 92. Find the five-number summary and the IQR.

notes.title: Finding a five-number summary
steps: Q1 is the middle of 3; 5; 7, which is 5.
Q3 is the middle of 10; 12; 15, which is 12.

notes.text: To compare two groups, compare a measure of **centre** (mean or median) and a measure of **spread** (range or IQR). For example: 'Class A had a higher median (68 vs 62), but Class B's marks were more consistent (IQR 12 vs 25).'

notes.label: Misleading statistics
notes.text: Watch for: graphs whose axes do not start at zero, small or biased samples, averages that hide outliers, percentages without the actual numbers ('sales up 100%' could mean from 1 to 2), and correlation presented as causation.

questions.prompt: To find out how much Grade 11s sleep, which sample is most representative?
options: Every fifth learner on the Grade 11 class lists
Learners who arrive first in the morning

questions.prompt: 'Wouldn't you agree that our school needs a longer lunch break?' is a leading question.
For the data 4; 6; 7; 9; 11; 13; 15; 18, $Q_1 = 6{,}5$ and $Q_3 = 14$. What is the IQR?
Team A: median 68 runs, IQR 30. Team B: median 61 runs, IQR 12. Compare the teams' batting performance.
questions.memo:
✓ Team A scores more runs on average (higher median) (1)
✓ Team B is more consistent (smaller IQR) (1)
✓ A sensible conclusion (e.g. A is stronger but less predictable) (1)

questions.prompt: An advert says 'Sales up 200%!' Why might this be misleading?
questions.memo:
✓ It gives no actual numbers (1)
✓ e.g. sales could have risen from 5 to 15 items, which is very small (1)

questions.prompt: In a box-and-whisker plot, the box shows…
A radio station asks listeners to SMS their opinion on a new taxi law. Explain why the results may be biased.
questions.memo:
✓ Only listeners of that station who choose to SMS take part (self-selected sample) (1)
✓ People with strong opinions are more likely to respond, so it is not representative (1)
